A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their full text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-prediction and robot-manipulation experiments on Open6DOR V2 and SIMPLER, component ablations, and an iteration-count analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds VLA comparisons, measured inference costs, and a ground-truth-versus-estimated-depth case study.

M1.justification: The evaluator–proposer loop, geometric techniques, context memory, pose updates, and system prompts remain unchanged. Clarifications of notation and canonical-object axis lengths do not alter the procedure. Estimated depth is tested as an input condition, without redesigning the method.

E1.justification: Open6DOR V2 and SIMPLER retain their existing task coverage. Appendix C adds a limited test scenario using Depth Anything 3 estimates instead of ground-truth depth, introducing imperfect depth inputs without adding a benchmark or task family.

E2.justification: Tables 6–7 substantially extend the robot-manipulation comparisons: π0.5 and GR00T are added on Open6DOR V2, and π0 and GR00T on SIMPLER. These are evaluated comparators, using specified fine-tuned checkpoints; all original comparators remain.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation protocols remain unchanged. Appendix B adds profiling over 1,616 position-task scenes, measuring calls per scene and per-call latency including rendering. Appendix C introduces the ground-truth-versus-estimated-depth comparison and specifies fine-tuned checkpoint settings for the additional baselines.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused efficiency analysis identifying the expensive pipeline stage and one depth-error case study examining downstream grasp failure. The component ablations, iteration-count analysis, and earlier qualitative examples are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 5 newly reports runtime distributions through means, medians, and 90th percentiles over 1,616 scenes. This adds descriptive statistical reporting. Neither version provides repeated-seed results, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark success rates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the iteration curves retain their values, but Tables 6–7 substantially expand comparative results. Open6DOR V2 overall 6-DoF manipulation success is 14.1% for the method, 2.4% for π0.5, and 0.6% for GR00T. On SIMPLER eggplant placement, π0 scores 70.8% versus the method's retained 66.7%. Table 5 adds measured latency results, and Figure 10 adds an estimated-depth failure outcome.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and their mathematical substance are retained. Renaming the initial scene from S1 to S0 and clarifying that fixed axis lengths use the canonical object's bounding box introduce no new assumptions, derivations, or formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract refocuses its robot-manipulation superiority claim from 'existing methods' to 'recent Vision-Language-Action models.' The principal claims about training-free closed-loop refinement and the three geometric techniques remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds a specific limitation: depth errors can shift perceived object height and cause an incorrect grasp despite a reasonable predicted goal pose. Appendix B identifies the predictor as the main latency bottleneck, making the previously general speed limitation more concrete.

D1.justification: Tables 6–7 identify the additional baselines' exact checkpoint variants and LIBERO or BridgeData V2 fine-tuning data, with associated resource references. v2 also names the depth estimator and documents rendering-inclusive timing. Existing system prompts and the project access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Depth Anything 3, BridgeData V2, and four checkpoint or repository resources supporting the new comparisons. The related-work discussion and positioning against scene-graph and simulator-assisted approaches remain substantially unchanged; the original π0 and GR00T papers were already cited.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized wording and notation clarifications, condenses the experimental overview, adds acknowledgements and appendix cross-references, and moves System Prompts from Appendix B to D around the expanded analyses. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–7 and the estimated-depth Figure 10, expands several captions, and moves Table 4 beside Figure 5. Existing visual examples and plotting formats are retained, while prompt figures are relocated and renumbered. The presentation changes are concentrated in the appendix and local layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v1 already supplied substantial benchmark and ablation evidence. v2 strengthens that foundation through comparisons with newer, explicitly identified VLA checkpoints, measured latency replacing a purely qualitative cost discussion, and a concrete depth-related failure explanation. These additions improve evaluation and transparency, although the depth investigation remains a single qualitative case and the new comparisons do not establish uniformly superior performance.
